Finding: No producer-scope AIMS AI policy yet; scope draft still needs leadership approval.
No AI impact assessments have been completed; methodology/template must be established and used.
AI-specific training is planned but not yet operating.
Existing classification taxonomy does not yet cover AI artifacts such as corpora, datasets, checkpoints, and delivered models.
AI-specific suppliers have not yet been run through the existing vendor program; supplier contract/DPA requirements are incomplete.
Some human-review and engineering practices operate in code/process but are not fully reflected in policy text.
Formal per-market AI regulatory/contractual mapping has not yet been performed.
No standalone AI/AIMS internal audit program or completed AI-scoped internal audit exists.
AI is discussed in quarterly leadership review, but a dedicated standing AI/AIMS review structure needs to be formalized.
No SoA exists; Annex A applicability and justifications must be decided and approved.
AIMS roles and responsibilities are not documented in a RACI.
No internal or external channel for reporting AI concerns or adverse impacts.
Model registry entries lacked an accountable owner field.
